name: set_thread_fault_code
prose: Static inline helper that updates the fault-code field of the current thread's flags. It computes ti->flags = (ti->flags & (~0 >> (32 - TI_FLAG_FAULT_CODE_SHIFT))) | (val << TI_FLAG_FAULT_CODE_SHIFT), with TI_FLAG_FAULT_CODE_SHIFT equal to 24. Here ~0 is the signed int -1, and on GCC right shift of a negative int is arithmetic, so the mask (~0 >> 8) is -1 (all ones) and the AND keeps every bit of ti->flags; the function therefore ORs (val << 24) into the flags and does not clear the previous upper byte first (the behaviour of the shift of a negative signed value is implementation-defined). Bits of val above bit 7 are shifted out of a 32-bit value. The function returns nothing, uses current_thread_info() and takes no lock.
note: Reviewers 1 and 2 (mask ~0>>8 is all ones, so upper byte is ORed, not replaced) RIGHT; reviewer 15 (code masks off the upper byte and replaces it) WRONG under GCC semantics (thread_info.h:157-158). Slice cut head; real function at 154-159.

name: rshift64
prose: Static inline helper returning a long long. If n >= 64 it returns mh >> (n - 64) (converted from unsigned long long to long long). Otherwise it returns (mh << (64 - n)) | (ml >> n), converted to long long. For 0 < n < 64 and 64 <= n < 128 every shift count is in 0..63; for n <= 0 the term mh << (64 - n) shifts by 64 or more, and for n >= 128 the first branch shifts mh by 64 or more, both undefined in C; the function does not check n. It touches no memory.
note: Contract removed (random testing showed it false: the old contract treated the result as a signed shift of the whole 128-bit value). Code at fpu.c:153-159. Slice cut head.

name: denormal_muld
prose: Multiplies two double-precision bit patterns when hx is denormal (SH-2A FPU emulation helper). It masks magnitudes ix = |hx| and iy = |hy|. If iy is below 0x0010000000000000 or ix == 0 it returns only the XOR of the two sign bits ((hx ^ hy) & 0x8000000000000000), i.e. a signed zero. Otherwise it takes exp from the exponent field of iy, ix as the mantissa of hx and iy with the implicit bit set, forms the 128-bit product with mult64 into (mh, ml), and finds w, the index of its highest set bit. It sets exp += w - 1022 - 52 * 2; if exp > 0 it builds the result as (rshift64(mh, ml, w - 52) & 0x000fffffffffffff) | ((long long)exp << 52); else if exp + 51 >= 0 it uses rshift64(mh, ml, w - 51 - exp) & 0x000fffffffffffff; else it uses 0. It ORs in the sign (hx ^ hy) & 0x8000000000000000 and returns it. It does not check that the shift counts passed to rshift64 are in 1..127 (for example w == 52 passes n = 0, a shift by 64 inside rshift64), and its own comment says guard bits are not used (FIXME).
note: Reviewer 15 (rshift64 can be called with n=0, shifting by 64 - UB) RIGHT: fpu.c:188,191 with w == 52 (or w - 51 - exp <= 0). Old precondition that all shifts are defined is false. Contract was empty. Slice cut head; real function at 161-197.

name: denormal_addd
prose: Adds two double-precision bit patterns when at least one operand is denormal (SH-2A FPU emulation helper), returning sign | ix. sign starts as the sign bit of hx, ix as |hx| and iy as |hy|. If the signs of hx and hy differ: when iy is below 0x0010000000000000 (denormal) it sets ix = denormal_subd1(ix, iy) and, if (int)ix is negative (a test on the low 32 bits of ix only), negates ix and flips sign; otherwise it sets ix = denormal_subd1(iy, ix) and flips sign. If the signs are equal: it sets ix = denormal_addd1(ix, iy) when iy is denormal and denormal_addd1(iy, ix) otherwise. It then returns sign | ix. Whether the low-32-bit sign test always detects a negative difference depends on the range of denormal_subd1's result (that helper was not read).

name: dwarf_cfa_execute_insns
prose: Executes the DWARF CFA instruction stream from insn_start while current_insn < insn_end and frame->pc <= pc, updating frame, and returns 0 at the end of the loop; it has no other return. It reads each opcode byte with __raw_readb. DW_CFA_advance_loc adds operand * cie->code_alignment_factor to frame->pc (the _loc1/_loc2/_loc4 forms read a 1, 2 or 4 byte delta and do the same). DW_CFA_offset and DW_CFA_offset_extended_sf allocate the register entry with dwarf_frame_alloc_reg and set its addr to offset * cie->data_alignment_factor with DWARF_REG_OFFSET (val_offset uses DWARF_VAL_OFFSET, GNU_negative_offset_extended stores the negated offset). DW_CFA_undefined sets DWARF_UNDEFINED; DW_CFA_def_cfa, def_cfa_register and def_cfa_offset set frame->cfa_register / cfa_offset (def_cfa and def_cfa_register also set DWARF_FRAME_CFA_REG_OFFSET); DW_CFA_def_cfa_expression records the expression pointer and length and sets DWARF_FRAME_CFA_REG_EXP. DW_CFA_nop, DW_CFA_restore, DW_CFA_offset_extended (computes but does not store an offset), DW_CFA_restore_extended and DW_CFA_GNU_args_size only consume their operands. Any other opcode prints a pr_debug message and invokes UNWINDER_BUG(), which is a BUG()-style trap, not an error return.
note: Reviewer 2 (unhandled opcodes return -EINVAL) WRONG: dwarf.c:545-548 there is no -EINVAL. Reviewer 15 (UNWINDER_BUG() is BUG(), so no skip/return 0) RIGHT (bug.h:80-107). Reviewer 1 ('always returns 0') right for non-trapping paths. Slice cut head; real function at 396-550.

name: BUILD_TRAP_HANDLER(bug)
prose: SH trap handler for the BUG trap (defined with BUILD_TRAP_HANDLER(bug); TRAP_HANDLER_DECL provides regs). It first rewinds regs->pc by instruction_size(__raw_readw(regs->pc - 4)). It calls notify_die(DIE_TRAP, "bug trap", regs, 0, TRAPA_BUG_OPCODE & 0xff, SIGTRAP) and returns if the result is NOTIFY_STOP. Then, when CONFIG_GENERIC_BUG is enabled and instruction_pointer(regs) is a kernel text address, it reads the instruction there, calls handle_BUG(regs) if it equals TRAPA_BUG_OPCODE, and returns in either case without sending a signal. In all other cases (not kernel text, or CONFIG_GENERIC_BUG disabled) it calls force_sig(SIGTRAP). It returns void.

name: main
prose: Host tool that patches a sparc a.out boot image. It requires exactly 5 arguments (otherwise it calls usage()), sets is64bit if argv[1] is "64", stat()s the boot image argv[4] (die() on failure), gets start and end from the System.map argv[3] with get_start_end (printing an error and exit(1) if that fails), opens the a.out file argv[2] read-write and reads its first 512 bytes (die() on failure or short read), and exits with "Not a.out" if the first four bytes are not the a.out magic. It then locates the "HdrS" header with get_hdrs_offset and seeks to offset + 10, fills a buffer with root_flags = 0, root_dev = 1, sparc_ramdisk_image = align(end + 32) and sparc_ramdisk_size = the boot image size, and writes 14 bytes of it (die() unless all written). For 64-bit it also seeks to offset 4 and writes a_text (computed from end, start and the boot image size) and zero a_data and a_bss (12 bytes). It then seeks to AOUT_TEXT_OFFSET - start + align(end + 32), opens argv[4] and copies it to the image in 1024-byte reads; a write that does not write everything calls die(), but a read() returning an error ends the copy loop silently. It closes both files (die() on close failure) and returns 0. Failures other than the read error end in exit with a message via die() or exit(1).
note: Reviewer 15 (read() error on the boot image is not checked; loop exits and returns 0) RIGHT: piggyback.c:256-258 'while ((i = read(...)) > 0)'. Slice cut head; real function at 177-265.

name: csum_tcpudp_magic
prose: Static inline function that returns csum_fold(csum_tcpudp_nofold(saddr, daddr, len, proto, sum)) as a __sum16: the TCP/UDP pseudo-header checksum computed by csum_tcpudp_nofold over the source and destination addresses, length, protocol and the supplied partial sum, folded to 16 bits by csum_fold. It has no side effects; the exact arithmetic is that of those two helpers, which are not re-derived here.
note: Contract removed: the old formula reimplemented csum_fold/csum_tcpudp_nofold and was rejected (reviewer 1: formula omitted the end-around carry). Code at checksum_64.h:85-90. Slice cut head.

name: pmd_mkdirty
prose: Static inline function that returns a pmd_t marked dirty. It converts pmd to a pte with __pte(pmd_val(pmd)), calls pte_mkdirty() on it and converts the result back with __pmd(pte_val(pte)). pte_mkdirty ORs the modified bit (_PAGE_MODIFIED_4U or _PAGE_MODIFIED_4V, chosen by instruction patching) into the value and, if the pte is writable (pte_write), additionally applies __pte_mkhwwrite, so other bits are not always preserved: the hardware-write bit may also be set. It has no other side effects.
note: Reviewer 15 (pte_mkdirty also sets the W bit, so not all other bits are preserved) RIGHT: pgtable_64.h:491-492. Slice cut head; real function at 748-755.

name: pmd_mkclean
prose: Static inline function that returns a pmd_t marked clean. It converts pmd to a pte with __pte(pmd_val(pmd)), calls pte_mkclean() on it and converts the result back with __pmd(pte_val(pte)). pte_mkclean clears both the modified bit and the write bit (_PAGE_MODIFIED | _PAGE_W, in the 4U or 4V encodings chosen by instruction patching), so other bits are not all preserved: the hardware-write bit is also cleared. It has no other side effects.
note: Reviewer 15 (pte_mkclean also clears the W bit) RIGHT: pgtable_64.h:512-513 (andn with _PAGE_MODIFIED_* | _PAGE_W_*). Slice cut head; real function at 757-764.

name: perfctr_irq
prose: Handler for the sparc64 performance-counter NMI (notrace __kprobes). It clears softint bit (1 << irq), increments this CPU's __nmi_count, calls nmi_enter(), and switches to the hardirq stack with set_hardirq_stack(). It calls notify_die(DIE_NMI, ...); if the result is NOTIFY_STOP it sets touched = 1, otherwise it writes pcr_nmi_disable to the PCR. It then reads sum = irq0_irqs; if the per-CPU nmi_touch is set it clears it and sets touched. If touched is 0 and last_irq_sum equals sum it increments alert_counter (so the counter is changed in this branch) and, when alert_counter reaches 30 * nmi_hz, calls die_nmi("BUG: NMI Watchdog detected LOCKUP", regs, panic_on_timeout); otherwise it stores sum in last_irq_sum and resets alert_counter to 0. If this CPU's wd_enabled is set it writes the PIC value (nmi_picl_value(nmi_hz)) and pcr_nmi_enable; when wd_enabled is 0 the counters are not re-enabled here, but in the NOTIFY_STOP case the PCR disable write was also skipped. Finally it restores the stack with restore_hardirq_stack(orig_sp), calls nmi_exit() and returns void.
note: Reviewer 1 (alert counter advances only if sum unchanged and not touched; otherwise resets) RIGHT. Reviewer 2 (PCR not disabled when notify_die returns NOTIFY_STOP) RIGHT: nmi.c:100-104. Reviewer 15 (alert_counter incremented in the lockup branch) RIGHT: nmi.c:111-113. Slice cut head; real function at 87-128.
